invariants: the Host contains no canonical domain capability inventory
new domains extend exact Lib packages instead of Rust or JavaScript Host APIs
WIT owns public domain semantics and the matching Lib owns its physical descriptor
the Host interprets mechanism, ownership and physical execution but not domain meaning
the full-host profile adds no per-domain grant or allowlist API

layers.name: contract

layers.responsibility: portable resource, operation, completion and window invariants

layers.name: runtime
layers.responsibility: fixed execution, ownership, scheduling and native descriptor machinery

layers.name: drivers
layers.responsibility: retained v0.0.15 domain qualification fixtures pending migration to Lib packages

layers.name: platform
layers.responsibility: retained platform qualification plus future domain-neutral native boundary executor

layers.responsibility: execution-environment implementation of the same domain-neutral boundary

layers.name: qualification
layers.responsibility: boundary invariance, unchanged-Host domain growth and lifecycle evidence

distribution_surfaces.extension_status: the extension array preserves v0.0.15 release-surface compatibility; target_extension is the unreleased successor
distribution_surfaces.rule: future domain growth occurs through exact Lib packages; packaging must not fork the fixed boundary

domain_model.physical_binding_authority: matching exact Lib package native boundary descriptor
domain_model.rule: domain and locality are Lib-defined semantics; neither creates a Rust Host API family

boundary_rules.irreducible_mechanism_exception: requires evidence across multiple independent Lib domains and a new architecture version

migration.target: file, process and network behavior supplied by Lib packages with one byte-identical Host binary

linux_native.convergence: one Lib-owned VFS/file-descriptor adapter reaches devfs, procfs and sysfs without device names or domain APIs in the fixed Rust executor
